mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates improving labor market conditions, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with positive PAYEMS growth (YoY > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7.0%, it signals a tightening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with UNRATE < 7.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals an active monetary easing cycle supporting economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of falling FEDFUNDS and rising INDPRO fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation environments (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%), the S&P 500 typically underperforms due to heightened expectations of aggressive central bank tightening and reduced real equity valuations, resulting in negative forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for residential construction, which typically correlates with broader economic expansion and positive equity market sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with rising HOUST (YoY > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) reflects a strengthening supply chain and manufacturing sector, which supports corporate profitability and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with INDPRO growth (YoY > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that typically suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.0, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending, which typically supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with rising RSAFS (YoY > 0).
